pr_title: fix(resolve): fix resolve cache to consider `conditions` and more
pr_body:
### Description

- closes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/18222
- fixes https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/16631 too

I simply expanded the cache key of "resolved cache", but I'm not sure if just concatenating everything is the best way in terms of performance.

_todo_

- [x] measure perf
  - https://github.com/hi-ogawa/reproductions/pull/41
pr_comments: _Run & review this pull request in [StackBlitz Codeflow](https://stackblitz.com/~/github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18302)._

I created a bench script with `server.pluginContainer.resolveId("some-package")` loop. https://github.com/hi-ogawa/reproductions/pull/41

Negative perf impact on `resolvePackageEntry` seems clear, but I'm not sure if there's a way to mitigate this. Can this per hit be considered acceptable?

<details><summary>cpuprofile viz</summary>

beta: [CPU.20241009.130606.40833.0.001.cpuprofile](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17301927/CPU.20241009.130606.40833.0.001.cpuprofile)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3894fed8-0f1a-42e4-baa8-f09bdd757cab)

this pr: [CPU.20241009.130349.39525.0.001.cpuprofile](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17301928/CPU.20241009.130349.39525.0.001.cpuprofile)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef889748-89c6-4cbd-b66c-4c9097deb3a6)

</details>

Maybe a simpler approach to split the cache for environment is to split `PackageCache`, which I think is currently shared at base `ResolvedConfig.packageCache`. 

I was testing css `@import` which uses `style` condition and I thought it would have the same issue, but it didn't on main. This made me wonder it's because css resolver doesn't use `packageCache`.

I was thinking we can instantiate a dedicated `config.packageCache` for each environment by proxying it here. Build is working but dev seems to have some issues. Is this approach supposed to work or packageCache should be still singleton?

https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/25868f2e68733530132b16639dea7165dba625e8/packages/vite/src/node/baseEnvironment.ts#L67-L80

I made `environment.config.packageCache` approach in a separate PR https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/18319. This seems like a sensible solution, but I need to double check if we can replace currently usages of `config.packageCache` nicely.

issue_context.title: `resolve.conditions` not working reliably on custom environment
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

I'm testing a custom environment like:

```js
  environments: {
    worker: {
      webCompatible: true,
      resolve: {
        conditions: ["worker"],
        noExternal: true,
      },
    },
```

and a package like:

```js
{
  "name": "test-dep-conditions",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "exports": {
    ".": {
      "worker": "./index.worker.js",
      "browser": "./index.browser.js",
      "default": "./index.default.js"
    }
  }
}
```

When importing such package both from default client environment and custom environment, custom environment side picks up `./index.browser.js` in some cases.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/hi-ogawa/reproductions/tree/main/vite-environment-resolve-condition

### Steps to reproduce

- open https://stackblitz.com/github/hi-ogawa/reproductions/tree/main/vite-environment-resolve-condition?file=src%2Fentry.tsx
  - shows `client: index.browser.js` correctly
- click `/worker` link
  - shows `worker: index.browser.js` but it's expected to show `worker: index.worker.js`
- go back and click `/custom1` link
  - shows `custom1: index.browser.js` but it's expected to show `custom1: index.custom1.js`
- kill server (Control+C) and restart
- click `/worker` link again
  - now it shows `worker: index.worker.js`
- go back and click `/custom1` link
  - shows `custom1: index.worker.js` but it's expected to show `custom1: index.custom1.js`

In this reproduction, I added three extra custom environments with and without `webCompatible: true`. ~It looks like the one with `webCompatible` has some mixed up resolutions depending on the order how they are resolved.~ It looks like resolution is cached by `webCompatible`, so for each `true/false` case, resolution depends on the order how they are resolved.

I also tested with the latest https://pkg.pr.new/vite@95020ab but the behavior seems to be same.

### System Info

```shell
(stackblitz)

  System:
    OS: Linux 5.0 undefined
    CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz
    Memory: 0 Bytes / 0 Bytes

    pnpm: 8.15.6 - /usr/local/bin/pnpm
  npmPackages:
    vite: 6.0.0-beta.1 => 6.0.0-beta.1
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

comments:
It looks like the issue is `setResolvedCache/getResolvedCache`'s cache key relying on `webCompatible`:
https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/95020ab49e12d143262859e095025cf02423c1d9/packages/vite/src/node/packages.ts#L28-L29

Similar issue about the fact that cache key is too coarse is discussed in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/12957#issuecomment-1546664484
This was broken before too then, in case `ssr.resolve.conditions` was different. `setResolvedCache` and `getResolvedCache` should be per environment, and not only keyed against `webCompatible`, no?

> This was broken before too then, in case `ssr.resolve.conditions` was different.

Probably so but maybe only when `ssr.target: 'webworker'` which makes both client and ssr `targetWeb: true`.

> `setResolvedCache` and `getResolvedCache` should be per environment, and not only keyed against `webCompatible`, no?

I haven't digested the other issue https://github.com/vitejs/vite/issues/12957#issuecomment-1546664484 but it looks like per-environment is not enough since there might be a case where single environment should resolve differently based on `isRequire` etc...

---

EDIT: I checked Vite 5 and indeed the issue is the same but only when `ssr.target: 'webworker'` https://github.com/hi-ogawa/reproductions/blob/main/vite-environment-resolve-condition/repro-v5.js

review_comments:
It is a pity that we couldn't use the environment instance as the key here. About the perf impact, did you measure the time to generate this key? Maybe we could avoid the array plus join and directly concatenate here.

Another option we could explore (maybe later?) is to have the `resolveCache` be created for each environment and pass that as an object in `options`, so we can directly do `options.resolveCache.get(key)` and avoid the key.

> About the perf impact, did you measure the time to generate this key? Maybe we could avoid the array plus join and directly concatenate here.

Yeah, I would imagine `getResolveCacheKey` is the factor. From the flamegraph, there is a stack of `resolvePackageEntry -> getResolvedCache -> getResolveCacheKey` and `getResolveCacheKey` is what's costly.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcf17f2e-4871-4b0c-be4a-ad1fa8b8eaf8)

> Maybe we could avoid the array plus join and directly concatenate here.

I tried to do some random tweak like this, but I didn't see much difference.

```ts
return (key 
  + '|' + (options.webCompatible ? '1' : '0')
  + '|' + (options.isRequire ? '1' : '0')
  + '|' + (options.conditions[0])
  + '|' + (options.conditions[1])
  + '|' + (options.conditions[1])
  + '|' + (options.extensions[2])
  + '|' + (options.extensions[2])
  // ...
)
```
